name: Emily
description: Emily runs a family-operated horticulture farm with her husband and three children. The farm depends heavily on reliable irrigation to maintain crop quality and protect permanent plantings. Changes in water availability can increase operating costs, disrupt production planning and place pressure on the family's main source of income.
goals: Maintain reliable access to water for crop production
Plan planting and production around expected water availability
Keep the family farm financially sustainable as the household's main source of income
concerns: Having to shift toward lower-water-use crops when allocations are uncertain
Securing enough water to protect permanent almond and citrus plantings during low-allocation periods

current.summary: Water allocations in the Murrumbidgee regulated river depend on licence categories and seasonal water availability. This profile assumes Emily holds a general-security entitlement, with a reported allocation of 45% as of 1 October 2026.
rules: General-security allocations are made after higher-priority categories have received their allocations.
Eligible general-security accounts may carry over up to 30% of entitlement; total account balance is limited to 100% of entitlement.
current.farmerImpact: Under the assumed general-security entitlement, Emily's 45% allocation would provide 45 ML against her illustrative 100 ML seasonal water requirement, leaving a 55 ML shortfall. At an assumed water purchase price of AUD 500/ML, purchasing the additional water would cost approximately AUD 27,500 before any proposed financial assistance.
current.title: Murrumbidgee water-sharing plans

name: Jamie Wilson
description: Jamie manages a orchard and vineyard. Permanent plantings need dependable irrigation even when commodity prices soften.

current.summary: The Victorian Murray system makes seasonal determinations for high- and low-reliability water shares according to available resources. This profile assumes Jamie holds a high-reliability water share, which is allocated before low-reliability shares; the Murray HRWS determination is 75% as of 1 October 2026.
current.sourceTitle: Victoria DEECA — How water is managed
rules: Seasonal determinations depend on available resources; high-reliability water shares are allocated before low-reliability shares.
Carryover may be held in spillable accounts when total allocation exceeds entitlement; spillable water can be unavailable until permitted and may be written off if relevant storages spill.
current.farmerImpact: Under the assumed high-reliability share, Jamie?s 75% seasonal allocation may leave less water for the modeled 100 ML demand. In the illustrative cost model, the 25 ML shortfall costs AUD 12,500 at AUD 500/ML before assistance. Carryover and spillable-account rules may affect usable water.
current.title: Victoria’s North and Murray water arrangements

current.summary: The Condamine–Balonne plan operates through water management protocols and scheme-specific operating rules. This profile assumes Casey holds a medium-priority entitlement in the St George Water Supply Scheme, where the 2026–27 announced allocation is 38% effective 1 July 2026. This is scheme-specific, not a Condamine–Balonne-wide percentage.
current.sourceTitle: Queensland Government — Condamine and Balonne Water Plan area
rules: Water access rules depend on the entitlement, water source and supply arrangement; scheme-supplied water is subject to the applicable operations manual.
St George medium-priority announced allocation is 38% for 2026–27, effective 1 July 2026; this figure applies to that scheme and priority.
current.farmerImpact: Under the assumed St George medium-priority entitlement, Casey's 38% seasonal allocation would provide 38 ML against an illustrative 100 ML water requirement, leaving a 62 ML shortfall. At an assumed temporary water purchase price of AUD 500/ML, obtaining the additional water would cost approximately AUD 31,000 before any proposed financial assistance. Water availability for purchase is not guaranteed.

current.summary: South Australian River Murray Class 3 (High Security) irrigators have a 100% allocation for 2026–27, announced 15 July 2026. Private carryover is unavailable for 2026–27 because the trigger was not met.
current.sourceTitle: SA Government — How River Murray water is allocated
rules: Class 3 high-security allocation reached 100% for the 2026–27 water year on 15 July 2026.
Private carryover is available only when the qualifying trigger is met; it is unavailable for 2026–27.
current.farmerImpact: Under the assumed Class 3 entitlement and 100 ML baseline demand, Morgan has 100 ML modeled available and no baseline shortfall. The model therefore estimates no additional water-purchase cost; future seasonal conditions may differ.
